name: Hollin
description: The Wardens' spare cob: a dun mare of fifteen hands with a hogged mane, a dorsal stripe and feathered heels, in the Wardens' green saddle cloth. Lent to the Foundling by Wren Tallow at Merrowby.

home.notes: tethered in the yard of the Toll's Lip, a few paces off its door

name: Nettle
description: Rosen Wyke's old forest pony: a grey-dun mare of thirteen hands, sure-footed on roots and scree, under a Woodfolk saddle-cloth of undyed wool. Rosen rode her as a girl and says she is too small for her now, which is not true.

look.notes: kin of the cob: the same forge body, smaller, greyer, with an undyed Woodfolk cloth

name: Kettle
description: The Wicks' old cart-horse: a dark bay mare of sixteen hands with a white blaze and heavy feathered heels, who pulled the eel-cart to Tollmere until the Tallymen priced the barrow off the Row. She is slow to start and slower to stop, and she has never once been frightened of anything, including the Lamp.

look.notes: kin of the cob: the same forge body, bigger, a darker bay, in a lake-blue Gullhithe cloth; the cob's feathered heels read as a draught horse's at this size

home.notes: in the Wicks' lean-to by the eel-racks

name: Tally
description: The Tallymen bravo's horse: a leggy bay mare with the Charter's brand on her near flank, under a brass-studded Tollmere saddle. Sauve says a horse with no rider is nobody's. Nobody has reported her stolen, because the one witness is the collector, and he is in the reeds with a very good reason to say nothing.

look.notes: kin of the cob: the same forge body, a redder bay, in a Tollmere cloth the colour of brass

home.notes: tethered at the landing's end; Sauve keeps her
